target_customer: Indian lenders, NBFCs, banks and businesses collecting loan repayments, subscriptions and fees via bank account mandates
problem: Businesses in India needed to collect recurring payments directly from customer bank accounts, but NACH mandates were paper based, slow and hard to integrate.
business_model: Usage-based fees per mandate and transaction on a recurring payments platform

founders.name: Atma Krishna
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CEO on the YC page; Juspay's release says he founded the company in 2016. Prior employers appear only in an aggregator snippet, so left empty.

founders.name: Dinesh Gadge
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page.

founders.name: Anand Krishna
previous_startups: Three-time founder per YC bio; currently building Inkle
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page, based in Bangalore.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating with bank and NPCI mandate rails, handling registration and debit flows and settlement reliably took careful payments engineering, though built on established schemes.

defensibility.rationale: Bank integrations, mandate registrations and compliance create stickiness, but payment gateways could add NACH on the same rails.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Juspay, a payments infrastructure company, bought it in February 2024 to strengthen recurring payments for BFSI clients, and kept it as a standalone service.

market_need_then: Lenders and subscription businesses needed automated debit collection; by 2023 LotusPay reported over 5 million mandates and over 20 million transactions per Juspay's release.

branding.domain_note: Uses lotuspay.com; domain history not found.

identity.visual_style: Enterprise fintech site with compliance badges
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct B2B, tagline Automate Recurring Revenue with eNACH

brand_strength.rationale: A pay suffix name with a lotus image that suits the Indian market, but no brand press found and similar names such as Lotus Pay exist.

outcome_analysis: LotusPay stayed small after YC, with a team of about five and only YC money visible, yet grew to serve lenders such as HDB Financial Services and InCred with millions of mandates by 2023. Juspay bought it for an undisclosed all-cash sum in February 2024 to deepen its recurring payments offering. The path looks like a capital efficient niche infrastructure company acquired by a larger payments player.
notes: Funding: aggregators say about 120 thousand USD total (YC standard deal) and an undisclosed seed in 2017-12; unverified and not recorded as rounds. Juspay release and Inc42 both say only that LotusPay was YC backed. Acquisition dated 2024-02-06 by Juspay and Inc42; YC page and one aggregator say January 2024. Founding year 2016 per Juspay release and YC; some profiles say 2017. A YourStory 2019 profile was blocked (403); founder education and prior employers therefore not recorded. No competitor coverage dated near 2017 found.
